questions.q: How much does a Chick-fil-A restaurant make per year?
questions.a: According to the QSR 50 Report, Chick-fil-A averages about $9.4 million in sales per unit, the highest in the industry. That's well ahead of other strong performers such as Portillo's and Raising Cane's. The brand gets there by generating more revenue from each store instead of chasing location count.

questions.q: Why does Chick-fil-A make so much money per store?
questions.a: Several habits work together: a high-throughput drive-thru, owner-operators who each run a single store, a tightly focused menu and an app that drives repeat visits. Dual-lane drive-thrus and outside order-takers let stores serve more guests per hour without cutting corners. A small menu keeps prep fast, kitchens smaller and waste low.

questions.q: What is sales per unit (SPU) in QSR?
questions.a: Sales per unit is the average annual revenue each restaurant location generates. It shows how productive your stores are, which unit count alone can't tell you. Tracking it as a core KPI pushes you to grow profitability in every location.

questions.q: How does Chick-fil-A's app increase sales?
questions.a: The app speeds up service through mobile ordering and rewards repeat visits with points. It lets the brand talk to guests directly, so it spends less on third-party advertising. It also collects first-party data that shapes decisions from store layout to upsell prompts.

questions.q: How can other restaurant brands copy Chick-fil-A's approach?
questions.a: Start by making sales per unit a core KPI and simplifying your menu so operations run faster with fewer mistakes. Study where your stores lose speed, and look at where automation or AI could help. Then invest in a first-party loyalty program instead of relying on discounts alone.
